Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  November 7, 2024

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio
  Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Parks Recreation and Community Service Director
  Juan Mata  Park Maintenance Supervisor
  Kaderick Burns  Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Human Services Program Manager

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Superintendent, Brian McClure reported on the
following: The City recently conducted a bidding process for the maintenance of swimming
pools at Edward Vincent Park. Bids closed yesterday, and we anticipate having a new
contractor in place by the beginning of the year. The City is in the process of finalizing a
contract with Joncowest for the cleaning of 14 park restrooms. This contract is scheduled
to commence on January 1, 2025. GRAFITTI ABATEMENT- Districts 2 and 4, as well as
Center Park and Edward Vincent Park, experienced a significant increase in graffiti this past
month. Additionally, we have added a Lead Graffiti Abatement Worker position to our
team. This position will provide supervision over the weekends. The Graffiti hotline is (310)
412-8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Mary Rouzan reported the following:
TURKEY GIVEAWAY - The City of Inglewood’s Annual Turkey Giveaway Presented by Pepsi
and Don Lee Farms will take place on Tuesday, November 21, from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Hollywood Park. The event will serve 2,500 Inglewood residents, providing turkeys
donated by Don Lee Farms, a bag of sides and additional items from Pepsi. This is a drive-
thru event and participants must be registered in advance to receive the items. No walk-
ups allowed. To register, call the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
at (310) 412-8750. HOLIDAY TREE LIGHTING CEREMONY - Please join us for this year’s
“Light Up Market Street” Holiday Fair & Tree Lighting Ceremony on Friday, December 1
from 4:00 – 8:00 p.m. in downtown Inglewood on Market Street. Please note this is a new
location. We invite you all to attend the special event that marks the beginning of the
holiday season. There will be live entertainment, refreshments and a special visit from
SANTA! New this year, the event will also include a snow play area, roller-skating rink,
food trucks, community organizations, and more. The entire community is encouraged to
attend this festive holiday event. YOUTH SPORTDS - For more information on our
Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website at
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Transportation Supervisor, Geoffrey Okamoto reported the
following: SENIOR CENTER ACTIVITIES AND PROGRAMS - The senior center continues to
increase in popularity, and October saw our fabulous Halloween party take place on
Tuesday, October 31. We are in the beginning stages of expanding our programs and
activities, with staff gathering information on classes and activities from senior centers all
over the region. We will be working closely with our Inglewood Senior Center Advisory
Committee to bring more valuable programming resources to our Senior Center than ever
before. NUTRITION - We serve approximately 450 seniors per week through home-
delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. We
continue to provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning
Institute. We are have been working with our seniors to develop new menus for the next
year and are looking forward to many new and exciting additions to our menu, including a
special Juneteenth meal. SENIOR TRANSPORTATION - Our paratransit program continues
to provide trips to seniors. Our I-Line Trolley starts at the Inglewood Senior Center;
operates Monday through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.
and takes an hour to make one full loop of all its stops. The trolley is free to the public. If
the public wanted the I-Line’s whereabouts during the day, they can contact the dispatch
office at 310.412.4378. We also provided transportation for seniors to our City’s Día de los
Muertos event on Saturday, October 28. CHILD AND ADULT CARE FOOD PROGRAM
(CACFP) - The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years
old and under and operates at Crenshaw Library, Inglewood Main Library, Rogers Park, and
Darby Park . The program's hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30
p.m. - 3:30 p.m. and snacks from 4:30 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. We serve an average of 115 suppers
and 50 snacks per week.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Director, Thomas Uwal reported on the following: EDWARD VINCENT
PARK ARBORETUM PROJECT - The arboretum renovation at Edward Vincent Park is nearly
finished, with new picnic shelters, tables, and concrete slabs in place. Once the final
checklist items are addressed, the arboretum will be ready to open to the public. The
project will be completed by the end of the year. SMINSKI PARK PROJECT- Most work at
Siminiski Park is now complete, and attention is shifting to the adjacent residential lot
recently acquired by the city. Staff continues meeting with Councilmember Morales to
explore development options that best serve and benefit the community. ANNUAL
INGLEWOOD OPEN STUDIOS EVENT - the Inglewood Open Studio Art Walk Program will
occur on Saturday and Sunday, November 9 and 10. The city will assist the event by
providing transportation and sponsoring the printing and installation of the street banners
advertising the Inglewood Open Studio Art Walk throughout the city. The Opening
Reception and Art walk kickoff will be on Friday, November 8, 2024, at Hyde Park Plaza,
630 N. La Brea Avenue, from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. The Mayor and Council are expected
to give their remarks at 6:00 p.m. INTUIT DOME THANKSGIVING LUNCHEON FOR
INGLEWOOD SENIORS - The Clippers are looking to host our Inglewood Seniors for a
Thanksgiving Lunch at the Intuit dome on Thursday, November 21, 2024. Our Human
Services Superintendent, Baz Devlia, is meeting and planning the logistics with Tracy
Schneider, Director of Community Relations & Player Programs at LA Clippers. Intuit Dome
also offered to provide transportation to the luncheon for our seniors. Seniors are signing
their names at the Inglewood Senior Center to attend the event.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. The owner, Maliaka Mitchell with Maliaka & Associates LLC, provided
flyers to raise awareness and express her interest in possibly collaborating with the city
through her organization, which fosters social inclusion for individuals with disabilities.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown announced a resource fair for
veterans at Chili’s on December 6 from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Commissioner Denmon
congratulated Teresa Estrada on her new position as Assistant Director for Parks and
Recreation.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at 6:57 p.m.
